title: Kummer regular-immersion fundamental classes and their operations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. For a regular closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, locally of codimension $c\geq0$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories, roots-of-unity twists and the compact-support right adjoints [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Regular means that the ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. There is a canonical supported fundamental class, equivalently a morphism
$$\eta_{i,n}:\Lambda_{n,Z}\longrightarrow i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}(c)[2c].$$
On an affine chart with regular generators $t_1,\ldots,t_c$, put $Z_k=V(t_1,\ldots,t_k)$ ($Z_0=X$, $Z_c=Z$); the image of $t_k$ on $Z_{k-1}$ cuts out the effective Cartier divisor $Z_k\subset Z_{k-1}$. On this chart $\eta_{i,n}$ is the composite, under the composition rule below, of the $Ri_*\dashv i^!$ transposes of the supported Cartier Kummer maps $c_{Z_k,\Lambda_n}:R(i_k)_*\Lambda_{n,Z_k}\to\Lambda_{n,Z_{k-1}}(1)[2]$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] for $i_k:Z_k\hookrightarrow Z_{k-1}$. In particular, for $c=1$ the class of an effective Cartier divisor $D$ is the transpose of $c_{D,\Lambda_n}$, whose composite with the unit $\Lambda_{n,X}\to Ri_*\Lambda_{n,D}$ is $+c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$; this fixes the Kummer sign. This formula is independent of the regular generators and of their order, and determines the global class. For $c=0$ it is the canonical open-and-closed restriction map, with the identity immersion giving $1$.

Under exceptional transitivity and addition of twist-shifts these classes compose: for regular closed immersions $Z\xrightarrow iY\xrightarrow jX$, $\eta_{ji,n}=i_n^!(\eta_{j,n})(c_i)[2c_i]\circ\eta_{i,n}$. They commute with flat base change of pairs, with open restriction, and with localization and strict localization via the canonical continuity identifications of supported etale cohomology. For every $N\geq n$, reduction $\Lambda_N\to\Lambda_n$ carries the supported class $\eta_{i,N}$ to $\eta_{i,n}$. The Tate-line comparison for this reduction is induced by $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ on roots of unity, with dual tensor comparisons for negative twists.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 2.1 (supported Kummer first Chern class), Definition 2.3.1 and Theorem 2.3.2 (regular-immersion class and composition), Proposition 2.2.3.1 (base change preserving conormal data), section 3.2 before Definition 3.2.2 (local and strict-local restriction), coefficient square in Proposition 3.3.1 and compatible cocycles in Proposition 3.3.2. Continuity is the supported version of Stacks Tag 03Q6 (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology); only affine ind-etale localizations of Noetherian pairs are asserted here.

proof.text: Construct the class globally, before choosing regular generators. Work on a component where the codimension is the constant c>0. By [lem-per-regular-flag-blowup-geometry] the conormal C=I/I^2 is finite locally free of rank c. Apply [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class] to the identity presentation C -> I/I^2 and define gamma_i=gamma_(i,C). This is an actual element of H_Z^{2c}(X,Lambda_n(c)), characterized by its injective blowup pullback G(Q_C). The supported-Hom isomorphism of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] realizes it as Ri_*Lambda_Z -> Lambda_X(c)[2c]. Transpose under the right adjoint of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] to define eta_(i,n). This construction is global and canonical: it does not assume that arbitrary derived morphisms glue from equality on open charts. Components of different codimension use this same construction with their respective c.

For c=0, a length-zero regular presentation means I=0 in a neighbourhood of Z. Thus the image of the closed immersion is also open. Define the supported morphism by inclusion of the corresponding constant-sheaf summand; its transpose is restriction to that summand, and the identity immersion gives 1. For c=1, I=O_X(-D) is invertible, so its blowup is X by [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso]. The construction has Q_C=-1, hence gamma_i=-e_D(I,1). The dual-line identity in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] gives -e_D(I,1)=e_D(O_X(D),1), and identifies this with c_(D,Lambda_n). Its composite with the unit is +c_1(O_X(D)) by [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Thus the construction has precisely the required Cartier Kummer sign.

source.place: Definition 2.3.1 and section 2.1; rank-one specialization of Definition 2.2.2.7

proof.text: Use the nested supported action of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] to write gamma_i gamma_j for the class in H_Z^{2(m+d)}(X,Lambda_n(m+d)) associated to Z -i-> Y -j-> X of codimensions m,d. Its statement identifies this product with composition of supported morphisms and, after adjunction, with exceptional composition. More explicitly the two successive transposes use the composite Hom bijection in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; its unit and counit formulas give i^!(eta_j)(m)[2m] composed with eta_i. Here ji is again a regular immersion, so gamma_(ji) is defined: near a point of Z choose an affine open Spec A of X on which Y=V(s_1,...,s_d) with s regular, and, principal opens forming a base, shrink it to D(g) so that Z is cut out in Y by the images of a regular sequence t_1,...,t_m. Localization is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so tensoring the injective multiplication maps with A_g keeps s regular [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] (the final quotient is nonzero as it contains a point of Z); then s_1,...,s_d followed by lifts of the t_k is a regular sequence in A_g with quotient the ring of Z, directly by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Consequently it suffices to prove gamma_(ji)=gamma_i gamma_j. Codimension-zero factors are restrictions of constant-sheaf summands, so the equality is the identity/restriction identity. In the remaining argument m,d>0.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.2, identification with supported cohomology on p. 234

proof.text: First take d=1. Put E=C_(Z/Y), F=C_(Z/X), K=C_(Y/X)|Z, k=c_1(K), and xi=c_1(O_P(1)); write S_E=sum_(s=0)^(m-1)(-1)^s c_s(E) xi^(m-1-s). All coefficients are pulled from Z when used on P. Apply [lem-per-regular-flag-blowup-geometry] to pi:B=Bl_Z X -> X: its exceptional divisor is P=P(F), its other Cartier divisor is Ytilde=Bl_Z Y, and P'=P(E)=P intersection Ytilde. They meet transversely; pi^*I_Y=I_P tensor I_Ytilde as framed invertible ideals; the ideal of P' in P is K tensor O_P(-1). These are exactly the hypotheses needed for supported ideal additivity and transverse Cartier interchange. Pullback on H_Z^*(X) is injective by [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class] applied to the regular immersion ji.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.3.2, Cartier case, pp. 236–237

proof.text: Let G_P denote the ideal-normalized exceptional operator on B. The identity pi^*gamma_j=-e(I_P,1)-e(I_Ytilde,1) follows from Step 2 and framed-ideal additivity. Multiply by pi^*gamma_i, using naturality and the projection formula in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The first term is G_P((-1)^(m+1)c_m(E)): indeed the restriction of gamma_i to Z is (-1)^m c_m(E) by [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class]. For the second, the blowup formula for i gives the inner argument Q_E=-S_E on P'. Transverse Cartier interchange moves G_P outside G_(P' in P); the extra minus from gamma_j cancels the minus in Q_E. On P the latter operator is multiplication by c_1(K tensor O_P(-1))=k-xi. Here supported-Hom identifies a class supported on the Cartier divisor with its operator, so the projection formula applies to each polynomial term, which restricts from P. Thus pi^*(gamma_i gamma_j)=G_P((-1)^(m+1)c_m(E)+(k-xi)S_E). This computation uses the actual operator domains on the common support P', followed by enlargement to P; it does not equate classes having different supports.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.3.2, alpha and beta and their common outer Gysin operator, pp. 236–237

proof.text: The same blowup construction gives pi^*gamma_(ji)=G_P(Q_F), where Q_F=-sum_(s=0)^m(-1)^s c_s(F)xi^(m-s). The exact conormal sequence 0 -> K -> F -> E -> 0 is supplied by [lem-per-regular-flag-blowup-geometry]. Whitney's formula of [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] says c_s(F)=c_s(E)+k c_(s-1)(E), with c_0(E)=1 and c_s(E)=0 outside 0<=s<=m. Substitute these coefficients: sum_(s=0)^m(-1)^s c_s(F)xi^(m-s)=(xi-k)S_E+(-1)^m c_m(E). Negating shows that Q_F is the argument obtained in Step 5. Apply G_P and the injectivity in Step 4 to obtain gamma_(ji)=gamma_i gamma_j when j is Cartier.

source.place: End of proof of Theorem 2.3.2, Cartan–Whitney identity, p. 237

proof.text: For arbitrary d>0, blow up Y in X. In the notation of [lem-per-regular-flag-blowup-geometry], P=P(C_(Y/X)), P'=P times_Y Z, i':P' -> P, and j':P -> B. The conormal-presentation kernels K and K' have rank d-1 and K'=i'^*K. Write z=c_(d-1)(K^vee), z'=i'^*z. Base change and excess in [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class], with the dual-bundle sign from [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities], give pi^*gamma_(ji)=z' gamma_(j'i') and pi^*gamma_j=z gamma_(j'). Generalized-class base change and the stated isomorphism C_(P'/P)=p'^*C_(Z/Y) give p^*gamma_i=gamma_(i'). The hypotheses of Steps 4-6 hold for i',j': over an affine open of Y on which C_(Y/X) is free, P is covered by spectra of polynomial rings, which are free and hence flat modules, so p is flat; tensoring the injective multiplication maps of a local regular sequence for Z in Y with these flat algebras [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] shows that i' is a regular immersion of codimension m, cut out by the same equations; j' is an effective Cartier divisor, and j'i' is regular of codimension m+1 by the lifting argument of Step 3. Step 6 applies because j' is Cartier, so gamma_(j'i')=gamma_(i')gamma_(j'). Associativity and the projection formula now yield z' gamma_(i')gamma_(j')=gamma_(i')z gamma_(j')=pi^*(gamma_i gamma_j). Injectivity with support Z, not merely support Y, in the generalized-class statement proves the equality on X. Step 3 converts it into the claimed exceptional composition.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.3 and its conormal diagram, pp. 234–235

proof.text: Let t_1,...,t_c be regular generators on an affine chart, with the successive quotients Z_k of the statement. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], multiplication by t_k is injective modulo the preceding generators; hence each Z_k -> Z_(k-1) is the indicated effective Cartier divisor. Induct on c. The empty flag gives Step 2's identity; for c>0, apply Step 7 to the first Cartier inclusion Z_1 -> X and the suffix regular immersion Z_c -> Z_1. The suffix has c-1 regular generators, so the induction hypothesis identifies its class with the corresponding suffix composite. Step 2 identifies the first class with the supported Cartier Kummer map; associativity gives the entire flag composite. Every flag therefore computes the globally constructed gamma_i. A different set or order of generators which is a regular generating sequence computes that same class. No assertion that every permutation is regular in an arbitrary nonlocal ring, and no derived gluing principle, is used.

source.place: Definition 2.3.1 and Theorem 2.3.2, successive Cartier consequence

proof.text: For a flat base change, check at stalks: if A -> B is flat and multiplication by t_k is injective on A/(t_1,...,t_(k-1)), tensoring this injection with B is injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Its tensor quotient is B/(t_1,...,t_(k-1)); thus the pulled sequence remains regular wherever its final support is nonempty. Empty pulled supports give the zero class. The degree-one isomorphism in [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] identifies the pulled conormal with the new conormal. The arbitrary-base-change formula for generalized classes therefore identifies gamma_i pulled back with gamma_(i'). The codimension-zero summand map has the same restriction identity. Open restriction is also immediate from that formula, since restricting I/I^2 to an open is the conormal of the restricted ideal. Via supported-Hom these are compatibilities of the normalized supported classes, not a claim of exceptional base change for every complex.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.1 and Definition 2.3.1; flat preservation of local equations

proof.text: For N>=n the geometric blowup and its conormal presentation are unchanged. The coefficient naturality in [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class] carries its defining pullback G(Q_C) at level N to the level-n pullback G(Q_C). Injectivity at level n then forces the reduced class gamma_(i,N) to be gamma_(i,n). For c=0 the summand map has this compatibility directly. The Chern coefficients and Kummer products have the same comparisons by [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] and [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The roots comparison is u -> u^(ell^(N-n)); [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies its tensor powers, and the dual/evaluation identifications give negative twists. Supported-Hom and transposition carry precisely this supported-class comparison to the eta notation.

source.place: Coefficient square Proposition 3.3.1 and compatible cocycles Proposition 3.3.2; naturality of Definition 2.2.2.7

proof.text: For continuity take a small directed affine system X_a over an affine chart of X, representing a localization or strict localization, and set Z_a=Z times_X X_a, U_a=X_a-Z_a. Its limiting pair is (X_infty,Z_infty), and X_infty is Noetherian: a localization S^{-1}A of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, every ideal being extended from A; for the strict localization at a geometric point over a prime p of the chart A, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] and [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] identify the neighbourhood colimit with the strict henselization of the Noetherian local ring A_p, which is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. Each U_a is qcqs because the ideal of Z_a is finitely generated; transitions on U_a are affine base changes of those on X_a. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] to X_a and U_a with the pulled torsion Tate sheaf Lambda_n(c); [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] supplies its pullback identification. The supported-Hom mapping fibre of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] gives the natural sequences H^{q-1}(X_a) -> H^{q-1}(U_a) -> H^q_(Z_a)(X_a) -> H^q(X_a) -> H^q(U_a). Their filtered colimit is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. In the comparison with the limit sequence the four ordinary-cohomology maps are isomorphisms. Exactness gives the middle isomorphism: lift a target supported element's image in H^q(X_infty), correct its difference by a lift from H^{q-1}(U_infty), and use the same argument for a kernel element. This is precisely the canonical supported continuity map, being induced by restriction of the mapping fibres. Thus the supported groups, with their actual comparison maps, have the asserted continuity identifications.

source.place: Supported extraction of Stacks Tag 03Q6, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology

proof.text: Finally identify the class under that continuity map. On a nonempty constant-codimension part with c>0, restriction of I/I^2 to a localization or a strict localization is the conormal presentation of the restricted immersion: the canonical localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and the strict-henselization structural map is flat by [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat], so Step 9 applies to the limit. Alternatively on an affine regular-generating chart the ideal and its conormal basis are the same finite equations after passing to every neighbourhood and to the limit. Apply generalized-class naturality in [lem-per-modified-blowup-generalized-class] both to the stages and to the Noetherian limit, with these identity conormal presentations. It says that the images of the original gamma_i are gamma_(i_a) and gamma_(i_infty); these equalities are compatible with every transition. Since Step 11's map is induced by those very restriction maps, it carries the represented class to gamma_(i_infty). The summand construction gives the same assertion for c=0, including an empty support. Step 8 identifies these classes with the actual Kummer flag composites. Hence localization and strict localization preserve the required normalized class under the canonical supported continuity identification.
